_comment: THE INLINE `code` NODE source contract, as ONE file read by every engine that renders an inline code chip (api/test/barkpark/portable_doc/render/inline_code_source_parity_test.exs, js/packages/react/tests/inline-code-source.parity.test.ts, internal/pdrender/inline_code_source_parity_test.go). Sibling of code-source-aliases.json, which governs the BLOCK-level `code` node; this file governs the INLINE leaf and the two contracts are deliberately different. Law: the chip body is `value` when that is a NON-EMPTY string, else the flattened plain text of `children`. Precedence is FIRST NON-EMPTY, never first-non-blank: a `value` of " " WINS and keeps its space (an inline chip is a leaf whose authored value is verbatim). Flattening a child: a string/finite number is itself, a map is `value` || legacy `text` || (recursively) its own `children`, a nested array recurses; anything else contributes "". A non-array `children` contributes "". Hand-authored; regenerate nothing.

cases.name: value-only (the canonical shape every first-party producer writes)
children-only, one text leaf (66 live paragraphs carry this shape)
children-only, leaf keyed legacy `text` rather than `value`
conflict: a non-empty `value` wins over children
an EMPTY-STRING value falls through to children
a WHITESPACE value does NOT fall through — first non-EMPTY, not first non-blank
a non-stringish value (a map) coerces to "" and falls through
several children concatenate with no separator
a wrapper child recurses into ITS children (markup folds to plain text)
a bare string child and a finite number child both coerce
a bare ARRAY child (flattened one level too shallow) recurses
no value and no children → the empty chip body (unchanged degrade)
